steps.name: Ursus Caravan Member
steps.text: The snow's getting heavier.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Guard
steps.text: C'mon, take a swig.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Member
steps.text: Pah. I still regret giving that Sami flagon over to that girl.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Guard
steps.text: Forget it. You'd be in serious trouble if the border guards found it.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Guard
steps.text: Besides, do you really believe that a few words inscribed on his drum and flagon are enough to keep someone safe?

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Guard
steps.text: In this land of ice and snow, the only thing that can protect us is vodka.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Guard
steps.text: —Well, now it's just vodka, anyway.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Member
steps.text: That's not what I meant.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Member
steps.text: It's just that... the night before the incident, we were all still sitting together and chatting.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Guard
steps.text: Yeah, I remember, the two of you had little sisters who are about the same age.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Member
steps.text: And he never got a chance to make up with her.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Member
steps.text: So just think of it as me feeling sorry for him.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Member
steps.text: *sigh* I know what it's like. People who've been fighting for so long have so much blood on their hands that they can never go home.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Member
steps.text: But in the end, even after telling us all those stories about his family squabbles, he never told us who they were fighting.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Member
steps.text: They gave their lives to save us, but we never even found out what happened.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Member
steps.text: I should've kept his flagon. Honestly, I don't know how else to honor the memory of these mysterious Sami, other than with something I can touch.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Member
steps.text: ...Hah, maybe I'm just being too sentimental over a bunch of Sami savages.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Guard
steps.text: ...Do you still remember what they said when we were chatting that night? That the Sami don't believe that death is the end.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Guard
steps.text: Like, say you think it's a completely windless night, but something still gets blown over. They'd call that the souls of the dead passing by.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Guard
steps.text: Not stupid, if you ask me.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Member
steps.text: Which? Me, or the Sami superstition?

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Guard
steps.text: Both.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Guard
steps.text: Alright. Time to call the others and get ready to do some business.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Guard
steps.text: The next tribe shouldn't be too far from here. I saw someone in the snow.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: Sami bestowed upon us snow and ice to cleanse us anew. Sami bestowed upon us mud and soil to inherit blessings.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: We wish not to leave, yet nevertheless travel down the streams of departure.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: May our loved ones return home, like drops of water returning to the river.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: May disaster be kept far away, in the lands you cannot protect.
The Sami Elafias lower their lanterns, bend down to scoop up handfuls of water, and sing along with the shaman in low voices.
As the ship of the dead slowly sinks, one by one, the oil candles are extinguished.
Darkness gradually spreads across the water.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: Even if you aren't a member of our tribe, you should still show some basic respect for our ceremonies.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: Put down your weapon, hunter with the black bow. Lower your head.

steps.name: Sami Wetlands Inhabitant
steps.text: (*whispers*) Look at that hunter over there...

steps.name: Sami Wetlands Inhabitant
steps.text: You've seen people like her in the northern icefield, right? Do you think she'll darken our fates–

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: ...'The more people speak of doom, the clearer it casts its shadow.'

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: So I will not speak of it.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: Someone else will. Eikthyrnir will. But we are absolutely not among those who have the power to speak freely in this land.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: This is your final warning, hunter.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: Or else we will be forced to take up arms.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: W-Wait, hold on! She's just standing guard!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Typhon, can't you explain? I'm sure they'll understand!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: ...Shh.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I feel it moving.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Out of the way, now.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Everyone, leave this place!
Half an hour ago...

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: We're almost there.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Phew... Finally, some good news.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Didn't think I'd be the one to end up seasick... Err, that is what this is, right?

spans.text: Didn't think I'd be the one to end up seasick... Err, that

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: But Gitano, didn't you say you've been away from the tribe ever since they moved? Then how do you know where the burial site is?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Look at the wooden fencing over there. It's a warning.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: In the wetlands, the waters where a tribe buries their dead are usually off-limits.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: The fencing serves not only to warn those who are awake, but more importantly, to remind those who are sleeping.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Because everyone meets their departed friends and relatives in their dreams. If they aren't careful, it's very easy to wander into these places.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I see, I see, fascinating! I'll have to note this one down too.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: (Takes notes) 'Be careful when dreaming.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hrmm...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: (*whispers*) Does that mean I'll get in trouble again if I want to do some research on these waters?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Hm. What do you have in mind?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: It's this here, a beacon. I want to set it up underwater so I can collect some data.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Hmm... You said before that this thing can track a location?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Yup.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Okay. Give it to me.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Gitano, can we stop right before that fencing? I'm also getting the sense that something isn't quite right.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Go ahead.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: ...Don't worry. I already foresaw your safety before we left at dusk.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Huh? Did I ever ask you to read my fortune?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: All I remember is eating way too much for lunch and ending up in a food coma right up until we boarded the ship...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: *sigh*... Nobody forced you to eat all that in one go.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: There were narcoleptic mushrooms in the soup. We often add a few when people are feeling anxious or uneasy.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Ehehe... It sure was tasty.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Anyway, thanks Gitano!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: But it's true that we never asked her for anything...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Not that it matters.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: So how do we set up this beacon?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Just toss it into the water, and it'll handle the rest automatically.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Toss it? With how much force?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: No, no force! Just, let go of it and have it sink on its own...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Welp, the beacon's up and running, and the signal looks solid.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: It has an effective range of about three thousand meters, so we can keep moving– Err, rowing the boat forward.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Alright. Now, how am I supposed to make sense of this... gibberish?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I'd also like to keep track of the beacon.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh, that's real easy. Way simpler to understand than all this Sami stuff!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Look – over here we have the most basic data: relative coordinates of the beacon's location, water depth, flow speed...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: But I'm sure you can figure all that out on your own just from experience.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: In other words, it's continuously moving around underwater.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: It's probably just oscillating back and forth due to undulations in the water flow. These devices have extremely precise positioning.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Specimen sampling comes next.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: My drones are a bit noisy when I put them to work, so I prefer to use this compact beacon to do the preliminary water quality sampling and analysis first.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: While it's made for scientific investigation, its analysis is based mostly on the water's potability. But in areas not many people visit, even this simple analysis can sometimes produce anomalous results.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Take a look–

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: —Hmm?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: ...The signal disappeared.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Think it might've gotten swallowed up by a huge scalecis?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Though, we did take that sort of thing into consideration when we designed the beacon. No ordinary wild beast should be able to damage its outer covering...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Gitano.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Alright, got it.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I'll handle the ship for you.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Wait a sec, are you going to do another divination?

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: But... how many times have you used your Originium Arts, between yesterday and today?

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Not enough to worry about.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Just think of it as me double-checking my work.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: (Tugs on Magallan's hand)

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Leave her alone.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Aww... Fine.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: The first time I met Gitano was when I was visiting Iffy at the Rhodes Island Medical Department.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: At the time, she was in a coma in a hospital bed, and was carted in by the other field operators. They all said her Arts take a heavy toll on her body...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Even more reason to leave her alone then.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: She sensed something, which is why she's trying to read your fortune before you leave.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: And I agree with her.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I've felt a lingering shadow here this whole time.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I don't know exactly what she's trying to double-check, but there's no point in trying to avoid an omen of calamity.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I just hope she finds whatever is giving her these strange premonitions.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: —Watch out!
The boat tilts sharply to one side, and Typhon pulls Magallan in close just in time to stabilize the ship.
Gitano falls heavily onto the deck, and an intense burst of Arts flashes through her crystal ball.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Gitano!

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: ...Phew.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: I'm fine.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: I'm not the same self-defeating, self-destructive person I was years ago. This is just... me trying my best.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Well, as long as you're okay! Let me help you up.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: ...However, try as I might, I couldn't find anything.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: What did you see in your divination?

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Fate. The fates of the deceased.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: But my divination has little in common with Sami's prophecies – it's merely a special kind of Arts. It cannot touch those who have passed.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Their fates are pitch-black. Nothing more.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Is that the same for everyone?

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: ...No, there's one who hasn't responded to me.
Gitano holds up her crystal ball. There is nothing inside it save for the candlelight reflected from the fleet ahead.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: He remains silent.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: That is no fault of the diviner's.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: We need to hurry and make our way to the front of the fleet.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: If I'm forced to draw my bow, the boat's going to rock a whole lot, and you two will need to keep it steady.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: W-Wait, back up! What's going on?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: The marsh is trying to drag us under.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: None are safe, living or dead.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: —What?

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Member
steps.text: We don't know a thing! We really don't, so spare us, please!

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Member
steps.text: The only one who does is that Liberi who went to Čappat alone. He's the one you're looking for!

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Member
steps.text: Those Sami died to save us! But we didn't know what else to do for them, except take their remains back to their hometown!

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: No, that's not what I'm asking...

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: When you took the bodies away, someone was bleeding black blood. Did you witness this yourself?

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Member
steps.text: Yes, I saw it with my own eyes.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: How could I make such a terrible mistake?!

steps.name: Sami Wetlands Inhabitant
steps.text: The ship! The ship of the dead... What are you doing?!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Using the waves to keep it from sinking any further.

steps.name: Sami Wetlands Inhabitant
steps.text: You–

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Turn the boat around, now.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: This funeral can no longer continue. I will protect you from the rear.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: Let's go.

steps.name: Sami Wetlands Inhabitant
steps.text: You... Are you sympathizing with the outsider too?

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: Maybe she's right. Or maybe she's finally lost her mind to the black bow. Either way, she poses just as much danger.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: Warriors, protect the fleet from front to back. Stay vigilant.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: Don't panic.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: Trust that Sami will protect our inner peace. Trust that calamity will never take it from us.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: The same goes for you two, Magallan and Gitano.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Hurry up.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Wait, Typhon... I'd like an explanation. I need an answer.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Is it the same as what I saw?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Too many soldiers from the north are buried here. Their contamination has accumulated, day by day, until it all melded together.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: And this time, the disaster might've taken some of the dead–

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: —I understand.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: ...My Arts are supporting the ship of the dead, preventing it from sinking. But that doesn't solve the issue.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: So don't look back.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: But—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Anything we can do to help?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: M-My drone has a combat module! If there's going to be fighting, I can help out!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: No.
The dark swamp surges up, and the disaster merges into solid entities that leap towards Typhon from the black waves.
For over a decade, she has seen the same dream again and again. A pitch-black dream.
The Sami say that while asleep, people can free themselves from the shackles of their corporeal forms and meet both the living and the dead.
Typhon has always known that if she could strip away the darkness covering her eyes, she could turn back and take one last look at her mother and father–
Yet, she has never seen anything.
Because a hunter only keeps her eyes on her prey.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Don't look back. That's all.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Stay behind them, and keep rowing the ship. I'll handle the rest.
Her bowstring is fully drawn. Ancient Arts converge into a single shaft. She takes aim.
The threats on the icefield are numerous. Extreme cold. Waves of snow. Ferocious beasts. Demons. And, in the stories of certain tribes, herself.
Typhon takes this for granted. She carries a contaminated black bow on her back. She was engulfed by the shadows and escaped from them. In the eyes of others, she walks closest to disaster.
Naturally, then, she should be the one to stand between those people and disaster.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Looks like I got the drop on you again.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Now, depart from the lands of Sami.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: —I'll pin you down!
The hunter raises her voice as if shouting into the empty marsh.
The bowstring vibrates, and the arrow hurtles towards the water's depths.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Whooooaaaa! The boat's rocking like crazy!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Wh-What just happened? Did something fall into the water?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: —Whoa, it got cold all of a sudden!
The hunter's cry receives an answer from the water's surface.
It is a soft murmur in the Sami tongue.
'Water withered, hard ice becomes.'
From the water's depths, it spreads out with the ripples of the falling arrow. In the blink of an eye, the swamp is engulfed in freezing cold.
All is calm, save for the constant crashing sounds from beneath the ice.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: ...Thank goodness, I made it in time.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Thanks, Simone.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Did you hear my footsteps?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Wherever you go, the snow follows. The wind told me this.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Also, you said you'd attend the funeral.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Haha, you guys... really do trust me.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Naturally. I have a good eye, both for the weather and for people.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Simone's here?! We're saved!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hmm, looks like everything's quieting down. Does that mean our predicament is resolved?

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: ...Not yet.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: No, no, no...

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Who– What are they? What are those things?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: *sigh*... I told you not to look back.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: They are shadows left behind by contaminated corpses.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: No! Don't come any closer... Those warriors buried beneath the water... Aren't they supposed to be sealed under the ice? Shouldn't they be... resting in peace?

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: The marsh... Why hasn't it calmed down yet?

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: I, I... AAAAAHH!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Close your eyes.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Magallan, hold her hand.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Give her a touch of reality. Just like, uh... just like you always do.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Then, steer the ship away.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh... Um, okay!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Gitano... Do you feel any better now?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: She's calming down.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Just like that, Gitano. Listen to me.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: It's normal to feel fear. But if you continue like this, you will be transformed too.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: We can seal the bodies, but we cannot seal the shadows that seep from them.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: So don't blame yourself, and don't force yourself to see things through to the end.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Your brother isn't at fault for this disaster, and you certainly aren't either.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: The disaster simply found us. Or perhaps, we found it.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Which is why it awakened.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Their ships can't move very quickly. How much time do we have, Simone?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Traces of contamination are still all around us. I have no way to tell.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Right, so this is why Sami warned the Frost Maple tribe that they had to move away.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I can already feel their presence becoming more and more clear.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Sounds are vanishing, colors are disappearing, and bodies are melting.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: But don't worry, it won't affect my aim.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: ...I've always meant to ask. Are you not afraid?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Afraid? Of what?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: —This way!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Good! That's it, Simone! Direct your Arts where my arrows fly!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I've pinned down one corner of the shadows. The black blood is oozing out slower.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: My next arrow will be marked with fluorescent fletchings for you.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (Chants softly)

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Nightmare that terrorizes innocent children... Begone!
Crack. Crack. Crack.
The ice beneath her feet splits bit by bit, yet the shadow before her eyes shows no signs of retreating.
Arrow and Arts sink deep into the darkness, the blackness flowing like ink through their consciousness and into reality.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Ah... You really don't show any fear at all.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Are you not afraid of the demons?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: You're not afraid that you'll fail, only to regret it forevermore?
Crack. Crack. Crack.
The energy from the Originium Arts seems to pour endlessly into the abyss. Santalla tries to repair the ice, but naturally, it does not respond to her.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: —Don't go any further, Simone! It's too dangerous!

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Only I am at fault. And the responsibility is mine.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: ...Huh?
A premonition. A moment of inspiration. A chill rises from deep within her bones, like a gust of wind from a place where no wind blows.
For some inexplicable reason, Magallan has the urge to turn around.
She wants to see Simone and Typhon's enemies. To check if they are alright.
But all she sees is darkness. An endless darkness.
She remembers the stories she has heard.

Someone was seriously injured in a fierce battle and fell into a deep coma with a high fever. He dreamt he was hanging from a tree, facing off against a pitch-black beast so massive he could not see the whole thing.
A branch pierced the top of his head, and the blood flowing down over his body froze into a sculpture of crimson ice. But the warrior neither moved nor blinked.
Ten days and nights later, the fierce beast retreated, and he awoke from his fever only to find himself lying in the snow, and the wound atop his head fused with a tree branch.
All Sami know this legend, and whenever they speak of experiencing Sami's calling, they will surely bring up this story.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: —Aaaaahh!
The endless darkness is suddenly torn to shreds by brambles.

Black waves surge from between the cracks of the fractured ice, and the corpses that had begun to melt together reach towards the land with countless hands, but dissolve before they can stain the snow.
Purifying Arts penetrate the fog and shadow, and an entire army of northern warriors emerge from beyond the fencing.
They stand in formation, waiting with weapons in hand. Only one of them crosses the fence to approach.
Brambles spread in the direction his warhammer points—growing, twisting, and forming a ring that isolates the evil spirits. He extends his weapon and the Arts of his soldiers follow.
With no hesitation, no fear of being contaminated, he strides towards the dead, transformed warriors whose faces are no longer distinguishable, and raises his warhammer high.
In a single blow, names both spoken and forgotten are dissipated all at once.
The bright moonlight reflects across the forest's fresh snow.

steps.name: Sami Wetlands Inhabitant
steps.text: Those are... Treescar warriors.

steps.name: Sami Wetlands Inhabitant
steps.text: Eikthyrnir has come.

steps.name: Sami Wetlands Inhabitant
steps.text: Thank you... You saved our lives.

steps.name: Sami Wetlands Inhabitant
steps.text: We didn't expect warriors of the north to come so far south, especially not so close to the Columbians.

steps.name: Treescar Tribe Warrior
steps.text: Eikthyrnir came here to rescue the Sami who had moved south. He just happened to arrive sooner because he received a request for help.

steps.name: Sami Wetlands Inhabitant
steps.text: ...I thought that rumor was false.

steps.name: Treescar Tribe Warrior
steps.text: Unfortunately, all the rumors about him are true.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: Only a few tribes lack Snowpriests, so you may recall that it has been more than a decade since anyone in our tribe has been touched by Sami's calling.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: When I first returned to my tribe from the north, it was precisely because we were unable to actively predict Catastrophes or anticipate the disaster. Facing crises from every direction, we had no choice but to retain more soldiers.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: Now, even survival is difficult for us. Continuing to head south, perhaps even leaving Sami lands, is but a desperate measure.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: Eikthyrnir, it is not for a lack of love for this land that we leave, but rather a matter of necessity.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: You harbor resentment in your heart.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: How could I ever resent the very Sami that has given us everything?

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: You cannot change my mind.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: We cannot back down.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: You have already experienced the demons' depredations of nature. Living and dead alike are seized all the same.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: Fate has thrust them upon the Sami, and we must face them and endure.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: ...You said the same, during the snowstorm back then.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: 'Do not retreat. Do not move. We will stop the snowstorm and block the disaster north of the Fjal Vetrtonn.'

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: After the November hunt, the snowstorm did indeed stop. The line of black snow never crossed the other side of the mountain.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: Then you understand why there is no need for any Samijod to flee. You merely speak for your tribe, as well as all those who are anxious because they cannot receive Sami's revelation.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: But what we advocate for is sweeping away that layer of fog completely.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: No, Eikthyrnir. What you're doing flies in the face of everything we've experienced in Sami, passed down from generation to generation.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: We all know why only the most elite warriors travel to the northern lands.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: When we become aware of the demons' traces, we become conduits for them. We fear, and as such our weak hearts become their seedbeds.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: The more who are aware of this evil, the harder the next battle becomes.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: Nobody is above fear, but anyone can conquer it.

steps.name: Ceremony-Conducting Shaman
steps.text: That takes thousands of battles!

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: Indeed, it takes thousands of battles.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: The mountains will once again become an indomitable line of defense, just as they were many years ago, before fear penetrated the hearts of the Sami.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: We will never leave, and the Sami will never die out. No matter how many generations we must stand guard, it will be the disaster itself that dies first.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Woohoo, I got a pic.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Of Eikthyrnir? What makes him photo-worthy?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: He's the most authoritative warrior of the north, in the hearts of the Sami.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: That'll be very important to know on future research expeditions!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Although... he doesn't seem like the most easygoing guy. But you never know, maybe someone will come along who really wants to partner with him?

spans.text: Although... he doesn't seem like the most easygoing guy. But you never know, maybe someone will come along who

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Besides, what he just said to the other Sami should be recorded.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: What the silent mountain warriors know about the icefield, as well as how they combat the disaster, are all valuable data!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: And what was that word they used for the disaster? And... Andsko...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: 'Andskotarnir.' It means 'enemy.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hmm... I feel like I've heard it before somewhere. Let me write it down for now.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: So basically, for the Sami, only the disasters from the icefield are considered enemies?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: *sigh*... If only we just could listen in, I wouldn't have to go through all this trouble of sending in a drone up close.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Luckily, you taught me some tricks about camouflaging yourself so you don't alert your prey–

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: —Whoops. It got shot down.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: But it should still be salvageable! Once we get to Čappat, I can probably find a colleague from Rhine Lab to fix it.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: ...Consider yourself lucky then.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hehe.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: By the way, you're clearly fighting against the same thing, but they treat you like an outsider just because of your weapon?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Mm. Black bow aside, it's probably because of Arges.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: A lot of people see her as a madwoman, as they're quite familiar with the Cyclopes who live in seclusion in the Fjal Vetrtonn.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: They believe that, as a Cyclops, she should never have walked out of that cave. Should never have made contact with so many people.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: (In Sami) One who foresees fate will easily twist the fates of others.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: (In Sami) One who... foresees fate... Ack.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: In their eyes, I am someone who's had her fate twisted. Like... branches that have been artificially grafted together.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Trees like that will not grow properly.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: But you seem perfectly fine to me!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Mhm. I think so too.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh, Simone.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Please, let me check if you two are okay.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: This birdbrain over here seems fine enough. She just won't stop bouncing around.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Ehh?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Do you disagree? You act as if nothing happened.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Well, I guess that's true.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Oh right, Simone.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I didn't have time to answer your question earlier. I'll do it now.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: —I am scared.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: ...Hmm.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: But when I'm on the hunt, I have other things to think about.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Where to aim. The speed of the wind. Deducing where my prey will be. When my head is full of these thoughts, I have no time to be scared.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I know that I must overcome, again and again. My resolve will never be shaken.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: But just now, when the ice shattered, if I'd been the one to fall through, then that too would be fate's plan.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: So are you able to calmly confront the torments of fate... because Arges shared her visions with you?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: No, she's never spoken of them.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Haha, that makes me feel better then. The tragic prophecies of a Cyclops should not befall a child like you.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Where's Gitano?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: She left by herself.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I don't know where she plans to go, but she said she'll send word to Rhodes Island once she's made up her mind.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: ...How unfortunate. There was something I wanted to tell her earlier.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: But she should already understand by now.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh right! Even though I don't know exactly what's going on, I need to thank you all for resolving the crisis! Gitano too!

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Wait, what did she do?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: She was already exhausted by her Arts. And given the terror caused by the disaster, she wouldn't have been able to do anything rash.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh, she sent a request for help to the nearby tribes yesterday.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Just earlier, she told me something in secret... that she felt a vague sense of worry and guilt, so she wanted to ask for help.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: —Hello there, Mister Snowpriest! Thank you and the other Treescar warriors for helping us today!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: You're all lifesavers!

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: Child of the Santalla tree, daughter born of the biting cold.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Please do not call me that.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: You went after the Ursus.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: ...So you can see everything.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: How did it go?

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: You once hesitated because you longed for the shade beneath the ancient branches, and failed to become a Snowpriest.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: If you still wish to live as the old tree's steward, then I have no further questions for you.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: My time is limited because of Oripathy.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: That is no reason for you to lose sight of your goals.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: You understand this well, daughter of the Santalla Tree.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: You understand the futility of revenge better than anyone else. It is precisely because of that futility that it becomes a never-ending task, one that requires a constant search for new lives to fulfill it.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: I... am just an outcast. Hardly worthy of your attention.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: No one has forgotten the young shaman who was born to command the wind and snow.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Then I'm sure you're quite disappointed now that you've met her in person.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Hatred and stone alike took root within this body. She was robbed of an eye, and naturally became blind.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: She is a warrior, just as in the legends of the past.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: 'Bjoda,' 'Andarsár.'

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: The will of the All-Father has warned us. All that you see serves as a warning.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: The mountains raised by Sami are not enough to protect us from the disaster. Our sole enemy encroaches on our land.

steps.name: Eikthyrnir
steps.text: Even so, will you continue to wander the icefield, aimlessly seeking vengeance?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Sorry... I need to go to Čappat with my companions.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Nobody's left.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: One more snowstorm, and these fragile houses will disappear.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: I only had time to see the ruined end. Is this fate showing mercy, or cruelty?

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Brother, I now know what you saw when you turned back.
The wandering Elafia sits at the water's edge.
She leans down, wanting to cup the water to her face to wash away the dirty melted snow.
When she approaches the surface, shadows block the shimmering light, and she suddenly sees a wine flagon at the bottom of the water.
She recognizes the aged flagon as well as the prayer inscribed on it.
'Bestow upon the Myrkwood sacred purity; O Travelers, retrieve your innocent sight, those eyes that discern fate.'
'Bestow upon my home a lasting tranquility; My people, the dreamland is silent as falling snow.'
Sleep now. For one day, we will finally be able to return to that peaceful dream.
